  CEREMONIAL MATTERS Mayor Gordo issued a proclamation declaring the month of October
  2024 as First Tee - Greater Pasadena Month, and expressed his
  gratitude to First Tee - Greater Pasadena for enhancing the lives of the
  youth through golf, promoting character development and core values.
  Sally Yeh Wong, First Tee Board Member, accepted the proclamation
  on behalf of the organization and thanked the City Council for the
  recognition and their support.

  Vice Mayor Madison requested that the meeting be adjourned in
  memory of Judge Haley J. Fromholz, longtime Pasadena resident, and
  spoke on Judge Fromholz's career accomplishments, impact on
  Pasadena, and his passion for education and the rule of law.
  SPECIAL ITEM  PRESENTATION FROM PASADENA CITY STAFF ON THE
L  IMPACTS ON POWER DISTRIBUTION AND THE CITY'S
  RESPONSE DURING THE RECENT EXCESSIVE HEAT EVENT
  David Reyes, Acting General Manager, provided introductory remarks,
  and introduced Stacie Takeguchi, Assistant General Manager, who
  presented a Powerpoint presentation on the recent power outages that
  occurred throughout the City due to the recent extreme heat event. She
  provided information on the City's powerplant, generators, and backup
  plans for emergency preparedness, and reported on the City staff's
  ability to work to restore power to residents in a quick and efficient
  manner, and responded to questions.

  In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry regarding the issuance
  of a Flex Alert, Jen Guess Mayo, Assistant General Manager, provided
  details on the Flex Alert process, which is controlled by the California
  Independent System Operator (Cal ISO). Acting General Manager
  Reyes reported that the City's Emergency Operations Center (EOC)
  was not activated during the excessive heat event but the Department's
  internal EOC was activated. Councilmember Jones thanked staff for
  their hard work and also suggested communicating important
  updates/alerts in other languages.

L  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding the rotating
  outages, Assistant General Manager Takeguchi, reported that protocol
  calls for conducting rolling blackouts on a tiered basis.

  Council Minutes  2  09/16/2024
   Councilmember Lyon thanked City staff for communicating with the
  public quickly, and also suggested adding information regarding
  cooling center locations in the City as part of extreme heat event alerts.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's questions regarding the
  impacts of rolling blackouts on skilled nursing facilities and community
  members will life-sustaining electrical devices, Varoojan Avedian,
  Assistant General Manager, stated that skilled nursing facilities are
  generally excluded from rolling blackouts as tier three facilities, for
  safety reasons, and households with life-sustaining devices are tracked
  by the Water and Power Department as tier two locations to lessen
  possible rolling blackouts. He also shared that the Department has
  utilized bill inserts, social media posts, and emails to remind residents
  to register their life-sustaining devices. Councilmember Hampton also
  suggested activating Dial-A-Ride services to help transport residents to
  cooling centers during extreme heat events.

  Vice Mayor Madison suggested providing direct updates to the City
  Council and their District liaisons, and to better utilize them as a
  resource to inform residents of urgent matters.

  Lauren Siegel, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City Council
  to address extreme heat protocols for other departments that may
  have workers out in the field and suggested that the Public Health
  department release a report on the impacts of extreme weather on
  health.

  Sam Berndt, Pasadena resident, spoke on the shortfalls of natural
  gas generation during heat waves and advocated for alternative
  internal energy technologies.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus of the
  City Council, the presentation was received and filed.
  PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City Council to place
  MATTERS NOT ON THE  a measure on the ballot related to policy oversight.
  AGENDA
  Olden Denham, Pasadena resident, advocated for changes to the City
  Charter to increase City Council oversight and accountability for
  Pasadena Police Officers.

  Alieka Monet Marcos, Pasadena resident, expressed frustrations
  regarding Centennial Place, her interactions with Police Officers, and
  provided other various comments.

  Guy Todd, Pasadena resident, requested City assistance with his
L  Section 8 housing voucher.

  Sneferu Hines, Pasadena resident, requested a meeting with the
  Mayor, and provided other various comments.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 31 letters, advocating for the City to
  establish reasonable campaign contribution limits for the Mayor and
  City Councilmembers and providing various comments on the matter,
  were received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council,
  posted online, and made part of the public record for this item.

  In response to Councilmember Rivas' inquiry regarding the definition of
  a "person" making contributions, City Attorney Bagneris and
  Councilmember Lyon noted that the municipal code defines the term
  "person" to include natural persons and other entities.

  In response to Councilmember Rivas' inquiry regarding the
  responsibility of notifying candidates to return excess contributions,
  City Attorney Bagneris noted that the responsibility would fall under the
  City Clerk.

  In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry regarding the trigger for
  self-funding, City Attorney Bagneris reported that the matter could be
  referred to a Council Committee, the Council could reconstitute the
  Charter Study Task Force to study further, or another task force could
  be created to review the matter.

  In response to Vice Mayor Madison's inquiry regarding additional
  review or changes to the proposed ordinance subject to the City
  Charter provisions, City Attorney Bagneris noted that the ordinance can
  be reviewed until the election results are certified.
